card.thesis: Same engine limitation as round 1: entry/exit are evaluated per symbol against that symbol's own bars, with no cross-sectional comparison, so this still cannot buy 'the strongest sector' or trade a spread -- there is no relative-strength or pairs logic available at all. What changed is the universe, and I used it deliberately. Round 1 forced 9 semiconductor names that correlated at 0.589 average; before assuming round 2's sector ETFs would fix that, I measured them: the 11 US sector ETFs correlate at 0.581 average pairwise over the trailing 259 sessions through 2026-02-13 -- statistically indistinguishable from round 1's semis. Sector-vs-sector rotation is not the diversification round 2 actually offers; equity-vs-duration and equity-vs-gold are. IEF correlates -0.110 with SPY, TLT +0.090, GLD +0.042 -- genuinely uncorrelated, unlike round 1's universe. I also checked the two pairs the brief named directly and neither survived: HYG correlates 0.824 with SPY (it trades like equity beta with a coupon, not a hedge) and HYG vs IEF is only 0.226, not a clean risk-on/risk-off inverse. International (EEM 0.738, FXI 0.522, EWZ 0.491 vs SPY) also correlates with equities more than the 'uncorrelated Brazilian equities' framing suggests, and EEM/FXI correlate 0.847 with each other, so an EM sleeve would not have added a second independent bet either. What I built: apply one absolute trend-confirmation condition (close above its own 50-day average, RSI(14) between 55 and 80) identically across 7 symbols spanning three genuinely different sleeves -- growth equity (XLK, SPY), defensive equity (XLU, XLP), and duration/gold (IEF, TLT, GLD) -- capped at 3 concurrent positions. I tested whether the cap can express real rotation by asking: on sessions where both SPY and XLK fail the trend condition (90 of 260, i.e. equity beta is not confirmed), does anything else confirm instead? GLD qualifies 74.4% of those sessions, IEF 42.2%, XLP 43.3%, TLT only 26.7%, XLU only 17.8%. That is a real, measured complementary relationship -- gold and the shorter-duration bond ETF tend to be in their own confirmed uptrend precisely when growth equity is not -- and it is the closest thing to genuine rotation this absolute-condition-plus-cap design can produce: not because the rule compares assets to each other, but because uncorrelated assets independently satisfy or fail the same rule at different times, and the position cap is what turns that into a forced choice instead of a redundant tiebreak. Universe order is the fill-priority tiebreak on days when more than 3 qualify at once (39% of sessions had 4 or more of the 7 qualify simultaneously): I ordered XLK, SPY, GLD, IEF, XLU, XLP, TLT deliberately -- XLK and SPY first because they had the highest measured qualification rates (52.7%, 61.9%) and the largest sleeve, i.e. the strongest measured trend persistence in this window; GLD third despite being a 'hedge' in the correlation sense because at 59.6% qualification and 24.9% annualized vol it behaved like a trending risk asset in its own right this year, not a passive ballast; IEF ahead of TLT because IEF's qualification behavior was steadier (35.4% vs 26.2%) and the two are 0.889 correlated so there is little reason to want both when only one slot is at stake; XLU and XLP last among the equity sleeves because their co-qualification with a failed equity signal was the weakest (17.8% and 43.3% respectively) of the candidates I measured. On volatility: this universe's spread is far wider than round 1's -- annualized vol ranges from IEF at 5.6% to XLK at 27.3%, and GLD, at 24.9%, is not the cash-like ballast its reputation suggests in this specific window. A single stop_loss_pct cannot fit both ends: at 8% it is roughly 1.4x IEF's entire trailing 260-day max drawdown (-3.5%), so IEF positions will almost never be stopped out and will instead close on the trend-exit rule or the 120-day time stop; the same 8% is well inside normal noise for XLK and GLD (median absolute 10-day move 2.98% and 2.70%), so it will bind there as an actual risk control. I am sizing for the volatile end and accepting that the stop is nearly inert on the quiet end -- the alternative, a stop wide enough to matter for IEF, would be far too loose to protect XLK or GLD. On the other side of these trades: cross-asset risk-parity and macro funds that rotate into duration and gold ahead of confirmation (this rule is a lagging, close-only confirmation and will always be later than a fund trading on rate expectations or positioning data); trend-following CTAs running the same signal faster or with vol-targeting this fixed-size card cannot replicate; and, on the equity sleeves, dip-buyers who re-enter before a 50-day average reclaim confirms and are already positioned by the time this rule agrees.
card.entry: close > sma(50) and rsi(14) > 55 and rsi(14) < 80
